title: focus_owner: keep the unhide path reachable and never hide the enforcer
objective: A Device Owner enforcement pass could put the device into a state it could not leave. Hidden packages drop out of the default PackageManager enumeration, so the allowlist sweep could never see them again and nothing could be un-hidden; and hiding the enforcer itself would take the escape hatch and the trigger with it. Both paths are unrecoverable from the device, so both are closed here.
acceptance_criteria: installedThirdPartyPackages() queries with MATCH_UNINSTALLED_PACKAGES so already-hidden packages remain visible to the sweep
A pass following one that hid apps reports a non-empty packagesToShow and can restore them
The exporter injects the enforcer package into both the day and night allowlists, so the decision layer never proposes hiding it
EnforcementRunner keeps the point-of-use skip for its own package, covering a policy asset rendered before this fix or hand-edited
python_pkg/focus_policy stays at 100% branch coverage, including the new export behaviour
out_of_scope: Changing which third-party apps the policy blocks
Any change to Device Owner provisioning or the escape hatch mechanism
verifier: python -m pytest python_pkg/focus_policy --cov=python_pkg.focus_policy (123 passed, 100% branch coverage); on-device: a pass that hid three apps previously reported 'hid 0, restored 0' and left them hidden permanently — see focus_owner/docs/profile-owner-verification-2026-08-09.md
